piano-2.subject: piano
piano-2.title: Follow the join on the keyboard
piano-2.intro: Choose a count and watch what the fingers do. The written clock is for 60 BPM; you advance it yourself. Use the main playback controls above when you want to hear the tune.

scenes.label: The repair: C–D | E–E
scenes.intro: Begin on count 3 of the first bar. The bar line adds no pause. Elapsed time here starts with this fragment’s C.

frames.heading: Count 3: press C with the thumb.
frames.explanation: Start one note before the troublesome D-to-E handover. The thumb plays C while the index and middle fingers are ready over D and E.

frames.heading: Count 4: release C and press D.
frames.explanation: The index takes D. Keep the same gap between counts as before. Prepare the middle finger for E while D is sounding.

frames.label: Next 1
frames.heading: Next 1: release D and press E.
frames.explanation: The handover has happened: D | E. The count has returned to 1, but there was no extra beat or pause at the bar line.

frames.heading: Count 2: release E, then press E again.
frames.explanation: The next E is a separate note. The key must rise enough to make a fresh attack, even though the pitch has not changed.

frames.label: Release
frames.heading: At the following 3, release the fragment’s last E.
frames.explanation: That completes four equally spaced notes: C, D | E, E. Put this small repair back into the full phrase at the same slow tempo.

scenes.label: The whole eight-beat phrase
scenes.intro: The labels show bar / beat: 2 / 3 means bar 2, beat 3. The first E is time zero. There are seven attacks over eight beats; hold the last E through the final 4.

frames.heading: Bar 1, beat 1: press E.
frames.explanation: Begin with the middle finger. Thumb, index and middle are already placed over C, D and E.

frames.heading: Bar 1, beat 2: release E and press D.
frames.explanation: The index plays the next lower white key. Keep the pulse steady as the melody moves down.

frames.heading: Bar 1, beat 3: release D and press C.
frames.explanation: This is the bottom of the turn. Keep the thumb ready so you can return to D without hesitating.

frames.heading: Bar 1, beat 4: release C and press D.
frames.explanation: The index returns to D. The middle finger is ready for the E across the bar line.

frames.heading: Bar 2, beat 1: release D and press E.
frames.explanation: The join is complete. Keep the same pulse; the bar line does not create an extra gap.

frames.heading: Bar 2, beat 2: release E and press it again.
frames.explanation: This E needs a separate beginning. Reusing a note name does not automatically mean holding the earlier note.

frames.heading: Bar 2, beat 3: start the final E.
frames.explanation: This is the seventh and last attack. The note will last for two beats, so prepare to keep the key down on the next count.

frames.heading: Bar 2, beat 4: keep that same E down.
frames.explanation: There is no fresh attack here. You are counting a second beat inside the note that began on 3.

frames.label: Next 1
frames.heading: At the next 1, release E.
frames.explanation: Six one-beat notes plus the final two-beat note make eight beats. The count continued while the last sound was held.

descriptions.subject: spanish
descriptions.title: Build the phrase for the message you mean
descriptions.intro: Choose a message to see its complete model. You can then inspect the verb and adjective separately. The lesson’s audio above lets you hear the masculine bored/boring pair.
descriptions.sceneLabel: What do you want to say?

scenes.label: I am bored — masculine adjective
scenes.intro: You want to describe feeling bored.

parts.job: The verb for this feeling expression
The masculine adjective form in this expression

frames.label: 1. Verb
frames.heading: Start with estoy.
frames.explanation: Estoy begins the feeling expression here. Decide that you mean I feel bored before adding the adjective.

frames.label: 2. Adjective
frames.heading: Add aburrido.
frames.explanation: Use aburrido as the masculine adjective form for this speaker. Changing the adjective’s o or a ending matches the speaker; it does not change bored into boring.

frames.label: Whole sentence
frames.heading: Estoy aburrido.
frames.explanation: I am bored. With estoy, this phrase expresses the feeling. Compare a soy version to hear how the intended message changes.

chess-2.subject: chess
chess-2.title: Inspect the trapped king’s three destinations
chess-2.intro: Black is to move. Tap a8, a7, b7 or b8 to inspect the attacks, or use the explanation buttons. The pieces stay in place while we work through the position.
chess-2.position: White: king c6 and queen b6. Black: king a8. Black to move.

scenes.label: The stalemate position
scenes.intro: First inspect the square the king occupies; then inspect each possible destination.

frames.label: Start: a8
frames.heading: The king on a8 is not in check.
frames.explanation: The queen on b6 does not share a rank, file or diagonal with a8. The white king on c6 is too far away to attack it. Keep this no-check finding for the conclusion.

frames.label: Inspect a7
frames.heading: A7 is attacked by the queen.
frames.explanation: From b6 to a7 is one file left and one rank up: a queen diagonal. Moving the king there would put it into check, so a7 is unavailable.

frames.label: Inspect b7
frames.heading: B7 is attacked by both white pieces.
frames.explanation: The queen on b6 attacks b7 up the b-file. The white king on c6 also reaches b7 diagonally. Either attack is enough to make this destination unsafe.

frames.label: Inspect b8
frames.heading: B8 is attacked along the queen’s file.
frames.explanation: Follow b6–b7–b8. Those intervening squares are empty in the actual position, so the queen reaches b8. The black king cannot move there.

frames.label: Conclusion
frames.heading: No check and no legal move: stalemate.
frames.explanation: All three destinations are attacked. Black has no other piece that could move, but the king’s current square is not attacked. Under standard rules that is stalemate, a draw rather than checkmate.
